what_happened: Scene: layout 10 (white/grey kitchen, geometric tiles), 4-element black glass electric range with front knobs; pan_7 (rusty cast iron, integrated handle) in an upper cabinet; target rear_left; shrimp in a soup plate left of the range. Stage 0 was clean and fast: grasp at 102 at the handle base (width ~0.055, hold 112-366), pan set on the rear_left element (0.012 m at 320) and released at 366 (0.078 m). Stage 0 complete 381 (it broke only while the gripper was near the pan, 'objects still at target'). Stage 1: after a short miss (511-522), the shrimp was grasped at 545 (lift 0.18 m) and carried over the pan; at 628-664 the fingers were above the NEAR rim of the pan, where the handle joins (wrist: shrimp at the bottom edge of the pan), and it released at 655. The shrimp landed on the rim/handle junction, half outside the pan (0.107 m from the pan centre; wrist at 2280 shows it on the rim), so stage 1 never held. Stage 2: the policy turned the task knob rear_left to 2.91 rad (1149-1248; element under the pan glows red), then hovered; at 2301-2306 it came back and touched the shrimp and the pan without lifting anything, and at 2752-2848 it also turned front_left to 2.26 rad. Stage 2 never held because the shrimp was not in the pan.
causal_chain: pan correctly on rear_left (381) -> shrimp released over the pan's near rim / handle junction (655) -> shrimp rests on the rim 0.107 m from the pan centre, not inside -> correct knob turned on (1248) but stage 1 condition missing -> fail
self_recovery: One late touch of the shrimp at 2301-2306 (lift 0.002), no real re-placement.
official_criterion_notes: Borderline in-pan check: the shrimp lies on the rim at the handle junction (0.107 m from the pan centre). Visually it is half outside, so the official 'not in pan' verdict looks right, but a slightly looser receptacle test would have counted it and the episode would then have succeeded (task burner on at 1248).
